hook.line: Don't use Claude Code unless you've installed these five plugins.
hook.visual: Yellow '5 CLAUDE CODE PLUGINS' title over the presenter; ASCII art resolves into pixel 'CLAUDE CODE' above; cut at 1.47 s to an installer card with arrows numbered 1-5.

beats.what: Callout spoken to camera; ASCII art assembles into pixel 'CLAUDE CODE' above the yellow title.
Cut to an animated 'plugin installer' card: numbers 1 to 5 pop in with arrows pointing at a code icon, progress bar fills.
Item 1: the orange pixel Claude mascot appears on white above a terminal with a looping particle swirl.
Provider grid card ('251 AI Providers') shows the routing idea at a glance.
'Switching model' card: model tiles swap while he says the usage limit runs out.
Item 2 (memory plugin): GitHub readme in the top half, his face in the bottom half.
Item 3 announced with a serif 'THE THIRD' heading and a pixel-font name card on white, full frame.
'THE FOURTH' card with a pixel 'CLAUDE CODE' app icon, then a mock setup UI.
'THE FIFTH' card: app-icon tile with the plugin name, then a task list beside the pixel mascot.
Back to his face full frame for the link-in-description close.

characters.enters: Pops onto a plain white card at item 1, centred above the terminal
characters.acts: Stands still as the brand marker while a particle loop animates below it
characters.exits: Hard cut to the provider grid

why_it_works: Negative callout ('don't use X unless...') challenges people already using the tool, so they stay to check their setup.
Every item opens with the same ordinal title card ('THE THIRD', 'THE FOURTH', 'THE FIFTH'), so the viewer always knows where they are in the list.
Custom-made explainer cards (installer, provider grid, model switcher) replace raw screen recordings, so each idea is readable in under two seconds.
Pixel-art type and the pixel mascot tie all cards into one look that matches the Claude brand.
weaknesses: Grey caption pills are small and low contrast against the white cards.
No zoom punches (0 per minute) and long talking-head stretches in the middle feel flat compared with the busy opening.
Link-in-description CTA is spoken only in the last 2 s, after most viewers have scrolled.
for_robert: Use a recurring ordinal title card for each list item and let Fred be the one who carries it in, the way this video reuses its pixel mascot as a brand marker that comes back.
